state:
Goal `core-zip` is reached: `bun nv proofs --verify --group 'Core\Zip'` owes nothing, and `entries`, `read` and `extract` each have about, examples, attack, bench, help and a Rust `covers:` test.
The attack on `extract` found a denial of service: `place` resolves each folder level by its full path, so one entry nested a few thousand folders deep costs time quadratic in its depth (4000 levels took about 28 s in a debug build). It is recorded as gap `nvs-stdlib/extract-resolves-every-folder-level-from-the-root` (milestone M12), and step 6 of `tests/hostile/core/Zip/extract/01-many-files-a-taken-name-and-a-deep-folder.nvs` carries its `proof: gap` marker, so the sweep counts that case as a known gap.
The examples, the attack and the bench of `extract` get their `fs` grants from an `nvs.toml` in their own directory, the way `Core\Request\Part::saveTo`'s do. The attack's also sets `[limits] max_decompressed = "4M"`.

items.text: **Make `extract` linear in folder depth** — resolve each level relative to the level above's handle, or bound the depth an archive may name; then take the `proof: gap` marker off the attack (`rule:testing/a-failing-proof-is-fixed-or-recorded`, gap `nvs-stdlib/extract-resolves-every-folder-level-from-the-root`). `place` at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/zip.rs:796`, its caller at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/zip.rs:1068`.

backlog: The depth gap is a security finding (a small upload holds a request for seconds) filed under M12 because no open milestone owns `Core\Zip`; the user may want it earlier — `data/gaps/nvs-stdlib/extract-resolves-every-folder-level-from-the-root.json`.
